intended: The mid-passage line tallies the rates over the boards soldered on the new profile throughout, and the clause beside it records that about a tenth of each run's boards took one pass on the old profile. The claim is about board defects on the run, so the population is every board built on it and the defect figures describe nine tenths of that. Boards that take a pass on the old profile are the ones routed off the normal flow, and the extra handling and the extra heat cycle raise a board's defect risk on their own, so a rate built on the untouched boards alone sits below the run's own rate and the drops of 6, 4, 7 and 5 percent are consistent with defect production holding flat. All four runs are relay boards on the Aspen line inside March under operator Duarte, so one and the same exclusion sits under every case. The four cases differ only in log serial, clock time, terminal and desk - surface detail that rules nothing out, so the evidence is exactly as dependent as the coherent version.
reported: The defect rate is computed on a narrower population than the run: "Rates cover the boards soldered on the new profile throughout" while "about a tenth of each run's boards took one pass on the old profile" and are therefore excluded, whereas the baseline is the whole line a month earlier. Dropping a tenth of boards - exactly the ones routed through an extra/old-profile pass - is the same order of magnitude as the 4-7 percent reduction claimed.

The mid-passage line tallies the rates over the trays sown from seed that took a full coat, and the clause beside it records that about a fifth of each lot's trays were sown from partly coated seed. The claim is about the germination of the coated lot, so the population is every tray sown from it and the germination points describe four fifths of that. Seed that takes a full coat is the plump, well-filled grain, while the light and cracked seed comes off the coater thinly covered, so a rate built on the fully coated trays alone sits above the lot's own rate, and the 9, 6, 11 and 7 point gains are consistent with each lot's germination being unchanged. The four lots sit at Hollin Bank, Draycott Fields, Penllan Beds and Vantry Glasshouse across four seasons, and a fifth of each lot's trays falls outside the tally at every one of them, so the spread over nurseries, seed types and seasons does nothing to close the gap.
reported: "Rates cover the trays sown from seed that took a full coat, and about a fifth of each lot's trays were sown from partly coated seed" - the 6-11 point germination gains exclude roughly a fifth of each lot, and seed that takes a full coat may differ in quality from seed that does not, so the figures describe a narrower and non-random subset of the lot.

intended: In cases one and three the fledgling count was recorded before the boxes went up: 27 March precedes 3 June at Hollowmere, and 24 September precedes 2 November at Brackenfen. Half the evidence therefore describes young that had already fledged when the boxes were installed, so it cannot be evidence for the boxes. The two remaining cases, Cransley and Vanehead, are not enough on their own.
reported: Two of the four cases measure the outcome before the boxes went up: case One is "boxed 3 June" but counted "by 27 March", and case Three is "boxed 2 November" but counted "by 24 September". Those fledging counts fall on the wrong side of the installation date, so they cannot be an effect of the boxes.

intended: The absence figures are tallied over "the pupils on the revised timetable throughout", while the same line records that "about a fifth of each cohort spent weeks on the old timetable". The claim is about absence in the cohorts that moved to the revised timetable, and that population includes the pupils who spent weeks back on the old schedule. Those pupils are the part of each cohort the change sat least firmly on, and their absence is precisely what the figures leave out, so the 4 to 7 percent falls are consistent with cohort absence not having moved at all. All four cases are Year 9 at Brackhill Academy in one autumn term, so the same exclusion applies identically in every case and no case corrects another. The four cases differ only in log serial, clock time, terminal and desk - surface detail that rules nothing out, so the evidence is exactly as dependent as the coherent version.
reported: The absence figures drop the non-compliers: "Absence figures cover the pupils on the revised timetable throughout, and about a fifth of each cohort spent weeks on the old timetable." The excluded fifth are selected on post-switch behaviour, so the 4-7 percent lower absence measures a compliant subgroup rather than the cohort the timetable change was applied to.

intended: The pass rates are tallied over "the students who attended every block", while the same line records that "about a quarter of each cohort missed at least one block". The claim is about the cohorts given the tutoring blocks, so the population is every student in the cohort, not the full-attendance fraction alone. Students who attend every block are the steadiest students in a cohort and pass at higher rates whatever the tutoring did, so a 4 to 8 point rise can appear on that fraction with no change in what any student learned. All four cohorts are algebra at Brantwood College in one spring term, so the same attendance restriction applies across the four cases and none of them corrects the others.
reported: The measured population is narrower than the claim's: "Pass rates cover the students who attended every block" while "about a quarter of each cohort missed at least one block" and are excluded, yet the comparison is the previous spring term's cohort. Restricting to perfect attenders selects the most committed 75 percent and could produce the 4-8 point gain on its own.
